migration.description: Add durable metadata for original conversation artifacts while storing their bytes in a dedicated file volume.

durable_state.description: Original artifact bytes survive process restart in a dedicated object directory; PostgreSQL retains the artifact identity, session/run association, content type, size, SHA-256, creation time, pending/ready/unavailable publication state, the exact private staging object and the reason for an unavailable publication.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL publication intent managed by the embedded Goose migration and immutable, verified files below a configured dedicated artifact root.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_version: Phase-one candidate before migration 00007; no earlier artifact metadata or file-volume state is supported.
source_compatibility_range.earlier_state: The absent table is treated as an unapplied migration; the candidate is not ready until migration 00007 commits. Session/Run ownership foreign keys are deferred until the E01 schema is published.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Create conversation_artifacts metadata with validated identifiers, associations, immutable content metadata, pending publication intent, ready/unavailable state and session/run lookup indexes.

progress_signals: Goose records migration 00007 before artifact metadata is read or written.
A successful upload reports the persisted metadata only after a pending intent is committed, final bytes are hashed, synced, linked without overwrite and marked ready.
Recover processes a bounded pending set under per-identity database coordination and records unavailable state for missing or corrupt bytes; it never invents replacement content.

An explicit identical retry may replace only never-ready staging-missing or staging-corrupt state after reauthorization, exact metadata and byte validation, final absence confirmation and a durable pending repair intent.
Metadata and Open expose only verified ready objects and revalidate the stored file size and SHA-256 before returning metadata or a reader.
Content classification retains raw envelopes and unknown fields under 4 MiB record, 64 MiB consumed-batch and 10,000-record limits; runtime JSONL input uses an owned cancellable io.ReadCloser.
pause_points: After the metadata migration commits and before the Server or Connector mounts the artifact service.
After each staged file has passed size/hash validation and before its pending intent is committed.
After startup/runtime recovery completes its bounded pass and before file publication/download admission.

recovery.faulty_release_recovery: forward-repair-by-a-new-program-version-and-new-ordered-migration; pending intents remain recoverable, ambiguous database outcomes never trigger destructive compensation, missing/corrupt bytes become explicitly unavailable, and only the narrow explicit retry transition may repair never-ready staging-missing or staging-corrupt rows

required_test_evidence: A permitted Put persists original bytes and ready metadata, and Metadata/Open remain available after database close and reopen.

Process interruption after staging, intent, repair intent, final publication and readiness, including lost database responses, is recovered by a new Store process without deleting potentially committed bytes.

Separate processes coordinate same-ID publication, repair and reconciliation; identical immutable retries converge, while conflicting association, metadata, content, final objects, unknown reasons and previously-ready loss cannot overwrite or resurrect a publication.

Size and SHA-256 mismatches, blocked or non-cancellable readers, malformed identifiers, traversal/symlink paths and unauthorized operations are rejected without exposing host paths or partial metadata; cancellation cleanup remains bounded and does not leave a copy goroutine.

R02 basic and unknown fixture content retains its raw envelope/payload and remains a non-executing classification fallback under the per-record, total-byte and record-count budgets; fixture-only sanitization does not rewrite runtime codec data.
Migration 00007 is recognized idempotently and is not automatically reversed; E01 Session/Run ownership foreign keys are added only by a later ordered migration after their schema exists.
